Under Passport & Visa Manual 2006, there is no restriction for renewal of passport before its expiry. Passport having full validity of 5/10 years can be issued to the applicants even if existing passport has not completed its validity. However, a statement mentioning the reason for obtaining a new passport before its expiry may be obtained from the applicant. The applicant may visit the relevant passport office along with required documents for renewal of his/her passport. The existing passport will be returned to the applicant after taking necessary action. The Online Passport Renewal Service. is available for both.

The applicant will go through the following. steps at Regional Passport Offices in Pakistan and Pakistan Missions abroad. for obtaining the Machine Readable Passport (MRP): Arrival of the Applicant at Customer Service Counter. Capturing of Photograph + Token Issuance with QR Code. Biometrics/Finger Prints capture. Verification as per Office Record. (ECL/BL). Interview and Decision by Assistant Director. Fee Payment via QR Code. Passport Delivery (Collection of Passport). The Regional Passport Offices in Pakistan where the. One Window facilitation desk.

has been launched, Step-2 to Step-5 as elaborated above, have to be processed at one desk. Step 1. – Arrival of Applicant at Customer Service Counter. The applicant will approach the customer service counter at Regional Passport Office. The applicant will be guided about the process flow of the System for applying for the passport. After having the requisite documents, the applicant will be guided to the Token Counter. Step 2. – Capturing of Photograph + Token Issuance with QR Code. The applicant will produce the original CNIC/Smart-Card/NICOP or Children Registration Certificate (CRC)/B-Form, in case of below 18 years of age, along with its copies. The Official will proceed with capturing of applicant’s data i.e. photograph, CNIC Number,. application type etc. QR Code based token will be issued to the applicant. The applicant should check his details on token i.e. Application type, Priority type, CNIC/CRC number.

In case of any discrepancy, he should immediately report to an official at the token counter, otherwise, the applicant has to go through twice to all the subsequent stages. Step 3. – Biometric Data Capture (Finger Prints). The applicant after obtaining token will approach the Biometric Counter as soon as his token number appears at Biometric Capturing Counter. The official at the Counter will capture his right thumb, right index finger, Left Thumb and Left index finger impressions. Step 4. – Data Entry. Provide your valid. mobile no. / email id. at Data Entry Stage, during passport applying process, to receive your passport status via SMS / email from. 9988 / Email Rabta Service. The applicant will move to the Data Entry Counters as soon as his token number appears on the Counter.

The official will enter all the required data of the applicant while the data entry screen will also be visible to the Applicant. In case of any modification in data, the Applicant should guide the official accordingly. After the data entry is completed Data Entry Form will be printed by the operator and will be presented to the Applicant for rechecking/verification. The applicant will verify all its contents by signing the form. The form will be delivered to the applicant for further processing. ANY CHANGE IN THE DATA SHOULD BE POINTED OUT AT THIS STAGE. ONCE THE INFORMATION HAS BEEN SAVED, FOR ANY MODIFICATION THE TOKEN WILL HAVE TO BE CANCELLED AND THE APPLICANT WILL HAVE TO GO THROUGH THE WHOLE PROCESS AGAIN. AFTER ALLOWING “GO AHEAD” THE DATA BY THE ASSISTANT DIRECTOR, NO CHANGE IN THE DATA WILL BE POSSIBLE. Step 5. – Verification as per Office Record (ECL/BL).

The applicant will approach the ECL/BL Desk having Form. The verification against Exit Control List (ECL) and Black List (BL) will be carried out and official on the desk will affix clearance stamp on the data form after checking the record. The persons borne on ECL or BL, their passport process would be stopped here until its removal from such lists, as per rules/SOP. Step 6. – Interview & Decision by Assistant Director. Finally, the applicant will appear before Assistant Director / Officer In-charge when his token number appears on the decision counter, along with all the relevant documents and Data Form. The Assistant Director/ Officer In-charge will interview the applicant and satisfy himself with respect to the National Status/credibility of the applicant. Upon his satisfaction, he will allow, “Go ahead” the case, otherwise he can ask for additional documents.

If required he will refer the case to Security Agency for determination of National Status of the applicant as citizen of Pakistan. The Assistant Director will defer the case of Applicant below 18 years of age and will hand over the printed form to the applicant for attestation of his data form, from a Government Gazetted officer. The attester will have to write his/her CNIC No./ Contact No. besides affixing by-name official stamp on the form. On production of data form (duly attested) the deferred token of minor will be allowed go-ahead. After allowing go-ahead by Assistant Director, the applicant may leave the Passport Office, as the process is complete, by taking token generated at Step 2.

In case the matter is deferred due to some additional documents or case referred to the Security Agency for determination of National Status by the Assistant Director/ Officer In-charge, the applicant may also leave the office, as the remaining process will be completed upon receipt of documents/clearance report from Security Agency. The applicant would be informed upon receipt of clearance report telephonically. Step 7. – Fee Payment via QR Code. After generating a QR-based passport token the applicant can pay their passport Fee by scanning the QR code through any digital payment platform,. e.g., EasyPaisa, JazzCash, Online banking, etc. After successful utilization of passport fee payment, passport will be sent to production section for further printing process. Step 8. – Passport Delivery (Collection of Passport). After successful completion of above stages:-. The applicant will visit the Passport Delivery counter along with Original Token, on the given date for passport collection.

The passport will only be delivered to the applicant himself/herself or his/her blood relative. The applicant will also be intimated about the status of their passport via. SMS service 9988. inside Pakistan, while the. Email Rabta service. will inform about the status of the passport to overseas Pakistanis, if they have given their correct Mobile No. / Email ID at the data entry stage. Passports dispatched from the Production facility for delivery to the applicants within prescribed processing period, can be tracked through SMS Service / Helpline but to reach their destination i.e. respective Regional Passport Office (RPO) or Foreign Mission (FM) they may take some shipment time. The Passport Act 1974, Passport Rules 2021 and Passport Amendment Rules 2021 regulate the issuance of passports. Passport Act 1974. Passport Rules 2021. SRO No. 1139(1)/2023/Passport Amendment Rules, 2021. regulate the issuance of passports. Passports are issued in two major types: Machine-Readable Passport (MRP). Each type is further divided into the following subtypes: Emergency Travel Document. 1. Ordinary Passport. Ordinary Passport is issued to all Citizens of Pakistan for travel abroad, subject to completion of all codal formalities. Requirements for Ordinary Passport. Passport Application Process. 2. Official Passport. Official Passport is issued in pursuance of. Passport Rules 2021. SRO No. 1139(1)/2023/Passport Amendment Rules, 2021. 3. Diplomatic Passport. The Diplomatic Passport is issued to dignitaries of the State and Diplomats in pursuance of. Passport Rules 2021. SRO No. 1139(1)/2023/Passport Amendment Rules, 2021. 4. Emergency Travel Document.

Emergency Travel Document (ETD) is issued to Pakistanis abroad in case of emergency, in order to travel back to Pakistan one time. For more information see. SOP of Emergency Travel Document (ETD). Click this link to check e-Passport Fee. Q-15- What is the difference between. Machine Readable Passport (MRP). Both are issued by the Government of Pakistan, but they offer different features and benefits.

This comparison highlights the distinctions and advantages of each type. Machine-Readable Passport (MRP). Introduced in 2004. Launched in March 2021. Machine-Readable Zone (MRZ): MRPs include an MRZ that can be read by optical scanners at passport control. This zone contains the passport holder’s personal information in a standardized format. The data page includes the holder's photo, name, nationality, date of birth, and other relevant information. MRPs have various security features, such as watermarks, holograms, and UV-visible elements to prevent counterfeiting. Primarily a physical document without embedded electronic components. This contains a microchip embedded in the passport cover, which stores the holder's personal data, including biometric information such as fingerprints and a digital photograph. Offers advanced security features including digital signatures, encryption, and public key infrastructure (PKI) to prevent unauthorized access and tampering. The microchip can be read by RFID readers at passport control, facilitating quicker and more secure verification.

Comprehensive Biometric Data: Stores more detailed biometric data than MRPs, enhancing identity verification processes. Benefits of MRP. Benefits of e-Passport. Recognized and accepted globally, facilitating international travel. Generally, less expensive to produce and renew compared to e-passports. Adequate security features that meet international standards, ensuring the document's authenticity and integrity. The embedded microchip and encryption make e-passports significantly more secure against forgery and identity theft. The contactless chip allows for quicker processing at automated border control gates, reducing waiting times. The inclusion of biometric data provides a more reliable method of verifying the passport holder’s identity, improving border security. While both MRPs and e-Passports serve the primary function of facilitating international travel and verifying identity, e-Passports offer enhanced security, faster processing times, and more reliable identity verification through biometric data.

MRPs, on the other hand, are more cost-effective and widely recognized, making them a suitable option for travelers seeking a basic yet secure travel document.
